diagnostics.message: Semicolon present; review for clause stacking.
diagnostics.text: All four tracked market readings fell materially. The AI Equity Index dropped to 30.7, while the share of covered companies with positive one-year returns declined to 58.3%; sector trading pressure and the median return weakened as well. Palo Alto Networks nevertheless surged after an earnings beat, higher guidance and a reported $4.5 billion AI deal. That company-specific gain does not alter the broader deterioration.

diagnostics.message: Semicolon present; review for clause stacking.
diagnostics.text: Computer and peripheral-equipment output growth rose materially to 12.0%, while capacity utilization reached 84.5%. Semiconductor output growth slowed materially but remained higher at 15.3%, with utilization at 74.4%. Semiconductors therefore still lead in output growth, while computer equipment operates at higher utilization. Reuters separately reported that TSMC tightened restrictions on producing AI chips for China as new U.S. rules closed a manufacturing loophole; that development concerns access to specific chips rather than the aggregate utilization measures.

diagnostics.message: Semicolon present; review for clause stacking.
diagnostics.text: The physical picture is more resilient, though not uniform. Computer and peripheral-equipment output growth accelerated materially to 12.0%, with utilization at 84.5%. Semiconductor output growth slowed materially to 15.3%, while utilization fell to 74.4%. Available records also list 1,556 data-center sites in development—about half the operating count—and 894 in the tracked active pipeline. A reported $24 billion Texas project received a permit, although its tax break was rejected; that is progress in approval, not evidence of completed capacity.

diagnostics.message: Semicolon present; review for clause stacking.
diagnostics.text: The economy-wide payoff remains unresolved. Nonfarm-business productivity rose 2.1% and real output 2.3%, but real hourly compensation increased just 0.6% while unit labor costs rose 2.4%. Business deployment also remains incomplete, with 24.6% reporting current AI use, and these aggregate figures do not isolate AI's contribution. Reuters reported that the Fed's Jefferson said AI was boosting inflation while its productivity effect may come in the future; that remains a policy assessment rather than a decomposition of current economic results.
